newsitem.title: USA: Accident closes Mississippi River at Baton Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Accident closes Mississippi River at Baton Rouge.

text.p: The Mississippi River has been closed while workers clean up after a string of 25 barges hit a bridge in north Baton Rouge late Monday, the Coast Guard said Tuesday.

No injuries were reported, but two rock barges sank, two were beached and one was missing, while a tank barge carrying a mix of benzene and gasoline capsized and was aground on the west bank of the river, the Coast Guard said.
An unknown quantity of petrochemical products had leaked, and local officials ordered a precautionary evacuation of residents and businesses, affecting fewer than 100 people, authorities said.
Ingram Barge Co. was the owner of the capsized barge.
Only tows with no more than two barges are being permitted to move in the accident area, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
"Judging from the number of phone calls we've gotten, there must be a lot of traffic backing up there just like on the freeway," he said.
Flooding north of Louisiana and heavy rains have created high water and swift current on the river. The cause of the accident was under investigation.
